question: Predict the secondary structure of an RNA sequence using RNAfold (with the -p flag to generate a dot-plot file), then visualize the square root of base-pairing probabilities as a square heatmap.

files.eval_guideline: Square heatmap with nucleotide positions on both axes and cells colored by sqrt(base-pairing probability); color scheme and styling may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The filenames are identical (human_tRNA_Phe_dp.ps.png). Both are PNG images of the dot-plot heatmap.
files.strategy_reasoning: The output is a PNG plot, and the guideline describes what it has to show (a square heatmap with nucleotide positions on both axes, colored by sqrt of base-pairing probability). It also allows the colors and styling to differ, so a semantic visual comparison fits best.

comparison_details.explanation:
Reference: an 83x83 base-pair probability heatmap from RNAfold -p. Positions are 0-based, the y-axis runs upward, the colormap is viridis, and the colorbar is labelled "Base-pairing probability" with a maximum of about 0.85. Candidate: the same 83-nt human tRNA-Phe matrix. Positions are 1-based, the y-axis runs downward (matrix style), the colormap is viridis, and the colorbar is labelled "sqrt(base-pairing probability)" with a range of 0-1 but a data maximum of only about 0.70.

Pattern match: after flipping the y-axis and shifting indices by 1, every dominant stem diagonal lines up, each with its mirror image across the main diagonal. Examples: 0-based i~4-9 with j~73-78 (candidate rows 5-10, columns 74-79); i~55-59 with j~63-67; i~18-26 with j~36-45; the stems near i~10-16 with j~22-30; and the medium-probability alternative helices around (40-50, 55-65), (60-70, 35-45) and (70-80, 0-15). The structure and the scientific message are the same.

Main difference: the strongest pairs reach about 0.85 in the reference but only about 0.70 in the candidate's sqrt-labelled scale, and 0.85^2 is about 0.72. Faint alternative pairings are also noticeably dimmer in the candidate. This suggests one image plotted the probability itself while the other plotted its square root (RNAfold's dot-plot file already stores sqrt(p)). Either the candidate mislabels p as sqrt(p), or the reference plotted the stored values without labelling them as sqrt(p). The plotted numbers therefore differ by roughly a square, which is a data-level discrepancy rather than styling.

Axis direction, indexing, title, and colorbar range are acceptable presentation differences. The candidate is a square heatmap with nucleotide positions on both axes and an essentially identical pattern, but the value-scale difference makes it partially rather than fully equivalent.
